description:
What is awkward: crate-jmap-contacts-server/src/card.rs:292-339 defines apply_jmap_patch — a 49-line private helper implementing path-based patching for ContactCard/copy. Meanwhile, /set update across the workspace uses jmap_server::json_merge_patch (RFC 7396 merge-patch with the bd:JMAP-sc1b.97 depth cap and the bd:JMAP-sc1b.87 absent-field regression tests).

The two implementations have divergent semantics:
 - json_merge_patch: RFC 7396, recursive merge, null leaf = remove, non-object values replace wholesale, NO array index traversal.
 - apply_jmap_patch: RFC 6901-ish JSON Pointer (no leading slash), splits on /, traverses through intermediate objects (creating empty objects on the way), array indices treated as string keys, replaces non-object intermediates with empty objects, null leaf = remove.

These two semantics will produce different results for the SAME patch input applied to the SAME card. A contributor who reads the /set code path and then the /copy code path will reasonably assume they share semantics; they don't, and the divergence is not documented anywhere.

Suggested rewrite: route ContactCard/copy's optional override fields through json_merge_patch as well. This means the copy spec must be a merge-patch shape (no path-flattening) — which is what the canonical mail-server's Email/copy does (it accepts mailboxIds / keywords / receivedAt at the top level, applied as a merge over the source). It's also what the existing test 'copy_applies_flat_patch_correctly' actually exercises (flat top-level keys, merge semantics).

Reducing to one patch helper:
 (a) Eliminates the divergence-between-set-and-copy gotcha.
 (b) Cuts 49 lines of bespoke, partially-tested code with three open correctness issues (see JMAP-qz9v.4).
 (c) Aligns with the canonical extension-server template — mail-server has no equivalent helper.

This is at minimum an elegance fix and at maximum a correctness fix once the apply_jmap_patch bugs are addressed.
title: apply_jmap_patch in card.rs duplicates jmap-server::json_merge_patch concept with divergent semantics — consolidate
